scope: Clocks, PLL and system research; configuration evidence and documented behavior remain separate from a runtime or silicon validation

rules.claim: Four quadrants each select 16 primary channels. The 56 MID DCC paths plus four central fabric-entry DCC paths are source connections, not 60 independent global channels per quadrant.
globals.json maps coordinates to quadrant, tap side/column and spine. nextpnr adds these relationships outside ordinary Trellis wire globalization; preserve raw wire and segment identities.
SPINE and TAP_DRIVE have directed configurable 1:1 buffers. They must not be converted to unconditional bidirectional connections.
DCCA has glitchless clock enable and a configuration bypass. Its stopped output is low; input and output steady-state levels alone do not define capture/release event ordering.
DCSC MODESEL=0 selects the configured handshake/gating mode; MODESEL=1 selects the non-glitchless path. SEL is two bits, and invalid/non-one-hot selections have mode-specific constant outputs.
The DCS guide requires both clocks to oscillate for glitchless switching; POS/NEG switching waits for respective source-clock edges. A static mux cannot reproduce the documented operation.
ECLKBRIDGECS is a non-glitchless 2:1 mux and needs ECLKSYNCB after it to reach the ECLK tree. A bridge consumes specific edge-clock resources on both banks of a side.
CLKDIVF supports 2 and 3.5, has asynchronous active-high reset, and ALIGNWD shifts alignment. ECLKSYNCB STOP controls a synchronized stop/start, not an immediate Boolean AND.

PLL input/feedback/output divider settings written by nextpnr use logical divisor minus one; coarse and fine phase settings are written directly. Reference bypass, feedback source, output enables and reset/standby/phase controls remain distinct settings.
A PLL spans PLL0 plus PLL1 at the upper corners or a BANKREF tile at the lower corners. Config fragments are one PLL state, and the BANKREF bank settings are excluded from PLL ownership.
OSCG user, configuration and SED clocks originate in the internal oscillator but have different dividers. Nominal frequencies are not a measured per-die oscillator calibration.

nextpnr maps OSCG DIV=128 to database label 127, writes both OSC.DIV fragments, and leaves the overlapping EFB1 CCLK.MODE group unchanged using _NONE_. The bitstream cannot recover distinct original parameters 127 and 128 from these writes.

The writer reads DCSMODE from cell attributes, while the public primitive and clock-constraint derivation use parameters. Current probes preserve the observed parameter-to-POS mismatch rather than treating the requested HDL parameter as the programmed mode.

Wake-up has four phases controlled by an internal or external START clock, sequencing GOE, GSR/GSRN, GWDIS and DONE. External DONE can hold off completion. Inputs, output drivers, register reset and memory write permission are distinct controls.
The sysCONFIG guide gives sequences 4 and 21. It does not specify the exact phase-edge timing relationship; do not invent physical delays from the phase table.

GSR has active-low/active-high/none configuration and separate sync mode. User GSR, configuration wake-up reset and power-up reset must be tracked separately until their resource-specific effects are established.

USRMCLK controls CCLK through its data and tri-state inputs. nextpnr warns about MASTER_SPI_PORT=ENABLE; the configuration controller and user ownership must not drive independently without an ownership model.

DTR output bits 5:0 are a temperature code, bit 6 is reserved zero and bit 7 is data-valid. DTR_TEMP is a simulation code parameter, not a CRAM temperature field or a proved linear Celsius conversion.
SED uses a serial configuration-memory scan and a 32-bit reference CRC. Its enable/start/force-error/status interface, clock selection, scan progress and reference data require distinct state.

PB1384 says distributed RAM is not excluded from ECP5 SED CRC and can cause false SEDERROR. The 2022 usage guide still says memory contents are ignored; retain the specific erratum and its mitigation as a source conflict.
START is documented as a macro for external wake-up clock selection. Its unbound site references are not evidence that the function can be omitted from the whole-chip scope.
Yosys declarations for these clock/system blocks are blackboxes. Parameter and interface checks or a placed configuration do not execute a behavioral clock/system model.

ECLKSYNCB STOP assertion stops the output low on the fourth falling input edge; release resumes on the fourth rising input edge. Coincident control/clock ordering and initial synchronizer state remain open.

The same sysCLOCK revision states about/within 16 ms for PLL lock at pages 40/42 but 16 us after standby at page 44. These values cannot be silently normalized; use an explicit digital lock profile pending device evidence.

The DTR waveform labels 70 us between start-pulse release and valid data, and the pulse is stretched internally for two clock cycles. This is a documented timing label, not a measured tolerance or calibration.

Native Chip retains ctrl0, ctrl1, sed reference and usercode when reading commands, but ChipConfig.from_chip/to_chip drops them; current Python binding exposes usercode but not ctrl0/ctrl1/sed, and the runtime bridge exports none of the four. Preserve the source stream alongside decoded CRAM.

SED guide page 11 prose for SEDFRCERR conflicts with its 0/1 table; the state table says 1 forces error and 0 takes no action. SEDERR is documented as sticky until SEDENABLE goes low. The ambiguity remains recorded.

open_questions.question: Validate special segment relationships at perimeter and unavailable TAP positions without flattening the clock network; native metadata alone does not prove all physical endpoint functions.
DCCA capture and release phase, stopped input behavior, mode bypass and central-DCC control legality; no unchecked latch implementation becomes a silicon oracle.
DCSC handshakes under POS/NEG, dynamic MODESEL, stopped clocks and invalid selections, including precise transition behavior beyond the steady table.
ECLKSYNCB/BRGECLKSYNC stop/start state and interpretation of fixed input-to-output bypass arcs when synchronizer mode is selected.
CLKDIVF divide-by-3.5 event pattern, phase after reset/GSR, ALIGNWD slip and edge-bank sharing.

PLL lock acquisition/loss, missing or irregular input clock, reset/standby/wake and invalid feedback settings; digital behavior profiles need explicit event policies. Same-guide lock-time conflict: 16 ms on pages 40/42 versus 16 us on page 44.

Documented phase-step falling edge, PHASESEL mapping and T_VCO/8 step are collected. Resolve wrap, load/register sequencing, output event scheduling, PHASELOADREG formula and glitch behavior; static/dynamic coarse formulas and guide diagrams are not yet a silicon oracle.
Resolve source inconsistencies in sysCLOCK diagrams (SEL[3:0]/CLK<0-3> in a two-clock DCSC figure) and PLL/public/writer defaults; use actual interface and observed CRAM separately.
Confirm hardware effect of all DCSMODE and PLL feedback/bypass codes independent of the tool's DCS parameter/attribute mismatch.
Input/output clock routes of upper DLLDEL and dedicated PCLK/PLL pins, mode-qualified ECLK paths and limits of conservative nextpnr clock placement rules.
Resource-specific distinction and ordering of PUR/startup reset versus user GSR, including disabled slice GSR and RAM write protection; related S01/L04/B08.
Bind START clock selection, wake-up sequence and GOE/GWDIS/DONE controls to bitstream/control-register data; current .config/CRAM bridge loses some command-stream metadata.
Measure OSC divisor-label aliases, especially 127/128, and parameterize nominal oscillator frequency/calibration instead of inferring a unique divider from ambiguous raw codes.

SED polynomial/seed/bit order, scan exclusions/progress and PB1384 applicability by physical die revision remain open. The expected reference is retained as native Chip.sed from LSC_PROG_SED_CRC, but is lost in text-config conversion and not exposed by current Python Chip bindings.

HY04 measured the initial/final 0x9E byte, busy restart, high-level hold and variable binary-count intermediates at one room-temperature condition. The Celsius table, other temperatures, width/phase-dependent latency and conversion details below the 40 ns observer resolution remain open. The documented 70 us waveform remains separate evidence.
JTAGG user-register instructions and TAP state timing, TDO edge/tri-state behavior and interactions with configuration and boundary scan; BSDL has private/undocumented opcodes.
USRMCLK/CCLK and shared configuration-pin ownership through MSPI, reconfiguration and user mode; distinguish package bonding and fabric port existence.
Complete bitstream transport/control state, CRC/error handling, IDCODE/usercode, security/readback and partial/transparent reconfiguration; preserve unsupported commands explicitly.

CIBTEST/CLKTEST/BREFTEST/PVTTEST remain functionally undocumented. BCINRD/BCLVDSO are documented dynamic bank controls for banks 2/3/6/7 (power guide pages 5-6), but their configuration, endpoint binding and disabled-input output levels remain open; see P05.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Route an identifiable clock through each quadrant, tap boundary and DCC mode; change CE in each clock phase and repeat with the input stopped.
hardware_cases.observe: Per-segment counters, output pulse continuity and held level with saved routes/CRAM.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Drive DCS with distinguishable clocks; sweep all SEL values, MODESEL and decoded DCSMODE; stop either source separately.
hardware_cases.observe: Output selection, high/low hold, transition handshake and restart. Program modes by recorded CRAM, not an unverified HDL parameter.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Compare ECLKSYNC mode/bypass with STOP transitions and ECLK bridge selection on both sides and bridge synchronizers.
hardware_cases.observe: Actual bypass activity, start/stop edge counts and bank fanout; preserve the fixed-arc discrepancy.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Sweep CLKDIVF 2/3.5, reset/GSR and ALIGNWD with phase-separated controls, then controlled coincidences.
hardware_cases.observe: Output periods, phase sequence, slip and resource sharing.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Measure PLL outputs for divider/phase/feedback/bypass variants; exercise reset, enable, standby, phase controls and missing input.
hardware_cases.observe: Frequency/phase relationships and digital LOCK/INTLOCK transitions, separately from analog jitter.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Observe startup and user GSR independently, hold DONE externally, vary START clock and preserve a RAM/FF fingerprint with an observer outside the reset under test.
hardware_cases.observe: Output enable, register initialization, memory write blocking and wake-up progression.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Measure OSC output/counter ratios for distinct raw DIV patterns and aliased logical labels, especially 127/128, on the same die.
hardware_cases.observe: Effective ratios and repeatability under stated conditions; do not assume nominal 310 MHz is calibrated.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Exercise SED enable/start/force-error with known configuration and distributed-RAM writes; keep the erratum mitigation and unmitigated case separate.
hardware_cases.observe: Status and scan duration, error persistence and RAM-induced false errors.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Capture DTR with controlled start widths and repeat requests while observing all eight bits.
hardware_cases.observe: Data-valid timing, reserved bit and code stability; temperature mapping requires a separate measured condition.
hardware_cases.observation: Three complete loads, 730 unique windows each; 1995 isolated conversions with pooled fall-to-final median 821 observer ticks. Nominal 2.5-tick correction gives 32.740 us. Initial/final 0x9E; no drift in three 601-reading, 60-second runs; retrigger restarts and holding high prevents completion. Raw intermediate codes/offsets vary.
hardware_cases.execution: Event kernel: compile::Board::dtr_code default 0x9E, 00 during high/conversion (nonuniform fall-relative count offsets), latest fall + 32.740 us; fast mode refused. This is not a Celsius or analog model.

hardware_cases.stimulus: Exercise documented JTAG user/boundary instructions, CCLK ownership and configuration reset through a controlled external transport.
hardware_cases.observe: TAP/user chains, TDO enable, shared-pin conflicts and metadata/state transitions; do not probe arbitrary private opcodes.
